Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark concentric-ring spots on older leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply mancozeb or chlorothalonil fungicide at first sign of symptoms.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, avoid overhead irrigation, ensure balanced nitrogen fertilization.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, rapid wilting in humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply systemic fungicide immediately; destroy severely infected plants.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use certified seed tubers, avoid excess irrigation, plant resistant varieties.

Potato___Healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

Aphids.symptoms: Small sap-sucking insects clustered on leaf undersides; curling, yellowing leaves and sticky honeydew leading to sooty mold.
Aphids.treatment: Spray neem oil for mild infestations, or a systemic insecticide such as imidacloprid for heavy infestations.
Aphids.prevention: Encourage natural predators (ladybirds, lacewings), avoid excess nitrogen fertilization, monitor regularly.

Army worm.symptoms: Caterpillars chew ragged holes in leaves and bolls; can defoliate plants rapidly in heavy infestations.
Army worm.treatment: Apply a Bt-based biopesticide or chlorantraniliprole while larvae are still small.
Army worm.prevention: Use pheromone traps for early detection, scout fields regularly, rotate crops.

Bacterial Blight.symptoms: Angular, water-soaked lesions on leaves that turn dark; blackened lesions on stems (black arm).
Bacterial Blight.treatment: Apply copper oxychloride spray; remove and destroy infected plant debris.
Bacterial Blight.prevention: Use acid-delinted or treated seed, avoid overhead irrigation, plant resistant varieties.

Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease or pest symptoms detected.
Healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

Powdery Mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on the upper surface of leaves.
Powdery Mildew.treatment: Apply a sulfur-based or wettable sulfur fungicide spray.
Powdery Mildew.prevention: Maintain adequate plant spacing for airflow, avoid excess nitrogen fertilization.

Target spot.symptoms: Circular lesions with concentric target-like rings on leaves, causing defoliation in severe cases.
Target spot.prevention: Rotate crops, remove infected crop residue, maintain balanced fertilization.

bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Yellowing and wilting starting from leaf tips; water-soaked lesions turning white-grey along leaf margins.
bacterial_leaf_blight.treatment: Apply a copper-based bactericide; drain standing water to reduce humidity around the crop.
bacterial_leaf_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, plant certified disease-free seed.

bacterial_leaf_streak.symptoms: Narrow, water-soaked interveinal streaks on leaves that turn brown over time.
bacterial_leaf_streak.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide spray at early symptom onset.
bacterial_leaf_streak.prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen fertilization, maintain field sanitation.

bacterial_panicle_blight.symptoms: Panicle sterility and grain discoloration; most severe under high heat and humidity during flowering.
bacterial_panicle_blight.treatment: No fully effective chemical control exists; remove and destroy severely infected panicles.
bacterial_panicle_blight.prevention: Avoid planting windows that put flowering during peak heat stress, use balanced fertilization, plant resistant varieties where available.

black_stem_borer.symptoms: Larvae bore into stems, causing deadhearts in the vegetative stage and whiteheads at heading.
black_stem_borer.treatment: Apply a recommended systemic insecticide (e.g. cartap hydrochloride) at first sign of infestation.
black_stem_borer.prevention: Use pheromone traps for monitoring, remove and destroy stubble after harvest, synchronize planting across the area.

blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centers and brown margins on leaves; neck rot at the panicle base.
blast.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, use treated seed.

brown_spot.symptoms: Small oval brown lesions on leaves and grain.
brown_spot.prevention: Ensure balanced fertilization (especially potassium), use healthy seed, avoid water stress.

downy_mildew.symptoms: Pale yellow streaks on leaves, stunted growth, and sporulation on leaf undersides in humid weather.
downy_mildew.prevention: Improve field drainage, plant resistant varieties, rotate crops.

hispa.symptoms: Beetle larvae and adults scrape leaf tissue, leaving white streaks along the leaf blade.
hispa.treatment: Apply a recommended contact insecticide (e.g. chlorpyrifos) at early infestation.
hispa.prevention: Clip and destroy affected leaf tips, avoid excess nitrogen, maintain field sanitation.

leaf_roller.symptoms: Larvae roll leaves lengthwise and scrape the inner leaf tissue, leaving white patches.
leaf_roller.treatment: Apply a recommended insecticide (e.g. cartap hydrochloride).
leaf_roller.prevention: Encourage natural predators and parasitoids, maintain balanced fertilization, remove weed hosts.

normal.symptoms: No visible disease or pest symptoms detected.
normal.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

tungro.symptoms: Yellow-orange leaf discoloration and stunted growth; a viral disease spread by green leafhoppers.
tungro.treatment: No cure once infected — rogue and remove infected plants; control the leafhopper vector with a recommended insecticide.
tungro.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, synchronize planting across the area, control leafhopper populations early.

white_stem_borer.symptoms: Larvae bore into stems, causing whiteheads at the reproductive stage.
white_stem_borer.treatment: Apply a systemic insecticide at first sign of infestation.
white_stem_borer.prevention: Use pheromone traps, destroy stubble after harvest, synchronize planting.

yellow_stem_borer.symptoms: The most common rice stem borer; causes deadhearts in the vegetative stage and whiteheads at heading.
yellow_stem_borer.prevention: Use pheromone traps, maintain balanced nitrogen, synchronize transplanting across the area.

Aphid.symptoms: Sap-sucking insects on leaves and stems; honeydew and sooty mold, and can transmit viral diseases.
Aphid.treatment: Apply neem oil for mild infestations, or a systemic insecticide such as imidacloprid for heavy infestations.
Aphid.prevention: Encourage natural predators, sow on time, avoid excess nitrogen fertilization.

Black Rust.symptoms: Dark reddish-brown to black pustules on stems and leaves.
Black Rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, sow on time, destroy volunteer wheat plants that can carry the fungus between seasons.

Blast.symptoms: Bleached spikes and grey lesions on leaves; spreads rapidly in humid, warm weather.
Blast.treatment: Apply a triazole + strobilurin fungicide combination at the earliest sign of symptoms.
Blast.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid late sowing, avoid rotating with rice in blast-prone areas.

Brown Rust.symptoms: Small orange-brown pustules scattered across the leaf surface.
Brown Rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, sow on time, monitor fields closely early in the season.

Common Root Rot.symptoms: Browning and rotting of roots and crown tissue, resulting in poor stand establishment.
Common Root Rot.treatment: Treat seed with carboxin or thiram before sowing; no effective in-season chemical control exists.
Common Root Rot.prevention: Rotate crops, maintain balanced fertilization, avoid water stress.

Fusarium Head Blight.symptoms: Bleached spikelets with pink or orange mold on infected florets; infected grain carries a mycotoxin risk.
Fusarium Head Blight.treatment: Apply a triazole fungicide (e.g. tebuconazole) at flowering.
Fusarium Head Blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, rotate away from maize or wheat residue, avoid flowering during prolonged wet weather.

Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease or pest symptoms detected.
Healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

Leaf Blight.symptoms: Irregular brown necrotic lesions on leaves.
Leaf Blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, maintain balanced fertilization, keep fields free of infected residue.

Mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal patches on leaves and stems.
Mildew.treatment: Apply a sulfur-based or triazole fungicide spray.
Mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid dense sowing, maintain balanced nitrogen.

Mite.symptoms: Tiny sap-sucking arachnids causing stippled, yellowing leaves; fine webbing in heavy infestations.
Mite.treatment: Apply a miticide (e.g. dicofol) or neem oil spray.
Mite.prevention: Avoid drought stress, encourage natural predators.

Septoria.symptoms: Irregular brown blotches with tiny black fruiting bodies on leaves.
Septoria.prevention: Rotate crops, plant resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen.

Smut.symptoms: Grain is replaced by black spore masses at heading.
Smut.treatment: No treatment once infected; treat seed with a systemic fungicide (e.g. carboxin) before sowing.
Smut.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed, treat seed before sowing, plant resistant varieties.

Stem fly.symptoms: Larvae bore into stems, causing deadhearts in young plants.
Stem fly.treatment: Use a recommended systemic insecticide seed treatment, or an early foliar spray if infestation is detected.
Stem fly.prevention: Sow on time, maintain field sanitation, avoid late-sown crop which is more susceptible.

Tan spot.symptoms: Tan-colored lesions with a yellow halo on leaves.
Tan spot.treatment: Apply a triazole or strobilurin fungicide.
Tan spot.prevention: Rotate crops, manage residue (the fungus survives on wheat stubble), plant resistant varieties.

Yellow Rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules arranged in stripes along leaf veins.
Yellow Rust.treatment: Apply propiconazole or tebuconazole fungicide at the first sign of symptoms.
Yellow Rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, sow early, monitor fields closely in cool, humid weather.

Corn___Common_Rust.symptoms: Small, round to elongate reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
Corn___Common_Rust.treatment: Apply azoxystrobin or propiconazole fungicide if infestation is severe.
Corn___Common_Rust.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, sow on time, monitor fields regularly.

Corn___Gray_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Rectangular grey-tan lesions bound by leaf veins.
Corn___Gray_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Apply a strobilurin or triazole fungicide at early symptom onset.
Corn___Gray_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Rotate crops, plant resistant hybrids, manage residue since the fungus survives on corn debris.

Corn___Healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green lesions on leaves.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Apply a fungicide (e.g. azoxystrobin + propiconazole) if detected early in susceptible hybrids.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, rotate crops, manage crop residue.

Potato___Early_Blight.symptoms: Dark concentric-ring spots on older leaves.
Potato___Early_Blight.treatment: Apply mancozeb or chlorothalonil fungicide at first sign of symptoms.
Potato___Early_Blight.prevention: Rotate crops, avoid overhead irrigation, ensure balanced nitrogen fertilization.

Potato___Healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

Potato___Late_Blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems that rapidly turn brown/black; white mold on undersides in humid weather.
Potato___Late_Blight.treatment: Apply a systemic fungicide (e.g. metalaxyl + mancozeb) immediately; remove infected plants to stop spread.
Potato___Late_Blight.prevention: Use certified seed tubers, avoid excess irrigation, plant resistant varieties where available.

Rice___Brown_Spot.symptoms: Small oval brown lesions on leaves and grain.
Rice___Brown_Spot.prevention: Ensure balanced fertilization (especially potassium), use healthy seed.

Rice___Healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

Rice___Leaf_Blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centers and brown margins on leaves.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen.

Rice___Neck_Blast.symptoms: Infection at the panicle neck causes it to break or produce blank grains — the most damaging form of blast.
Rice___Neck_Blast.treatment: Apply tricyclazole or azoxystrobin fungicide at the booting-to-heading stage.
Rice___Neck_Blast.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, maintain balanced nitrogen, use treated seed.

Sugarcane_Bacterial Blight.symptoms: Elongated, water-soaked to reddish-brown streaks along leaves.
Sugarcane_Bacterial Blight.treatment: Remove and destroy infected clumps; copper-based bactericide as a supportive measure.
Sugarcane_Bacterial Blight.prevention: Use disease-free planting material, avoid waterlogging, plant resistant varieties.

Sugarcane_Healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

Sugarcane_Red Rot.symptoms: Reddish discoloration inside the stalk with white cross-bands; wilting and drying leaves.
Sugarcane_Red Rot.treatment: No effective in-season chemical cure; rogue and destroy infected clumps immediately.
Sugarcane_Red Rot.prevention: Use disease-free/resistant seed cane, rotate crops, avoid waterlogging, maintain field sanitation.

Wheat___Brown_Rust.symptoms: Small orange-brown pustules scattered across the leaf surface.
Wheat___Brown_Rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, sow on time.

Wheat___Healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization.

Wheat___Yellow_Rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules arranged in stripes along leaf veins.
Wheat___Yellow_Rust.treatment: Apply propiconazole or tebuconazole fungicide at the first sign of symptoms.
Wheat___Yellow_Rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, sow early, monitor fields closely in cool, humid weather.
